response.sql: WITH patient_stats AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic, AVG(HGB / HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS overall_ratio FROM patient_stats), above AS (SELECT p.ID, p.avg_pic, p.ratio FROM patient_stats p, overall o WHERE p.ratio > o.overall_ratio) SELECT AVG(avg_pic) AS avg_of_avg_pic, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(ratio - (SELECT overall_ratio FROM overall)) AS avg_excess_over_overall FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: Each patient's ratio is the mean of their per-record HGB/HCT values, with NULL records ignored by AVG. Records where HCT is 0 or NULL yield a NULL ratio in SQLite and are skipped the same way.

The all-patient average is the mean of the per-patient ratios, not the mean over all individual lab records, as the request says 'average of all patients' ratios'. Patients with no valid ratio are excluded from that average and cannot pass the filter.

The 'average amount by which ratios exceed' is the mean of (patient ratio minus the all-patient average) over the kept patients. Patients whose PIC values are all NULL are left out of the average of average PIC values.
